answer: Sybil resistance can rest on custody, not fees. Registration gives each identity a distinct 64 KB shard encrypted under its key, so two accounts cannot share a copy. Holders must answer probes at random times: each carries a one-time nonce and must return signed within two seconds. Renting a thousand aliases therefore pays for a thousand warm replicas on fast media, since shards parked in glacier-tier archives miss the window and count absent, and each miss burns deposit. The registry publishes an echo of every round-trip, and a kernel-level counter flags accounts spawned inside one machine.
